:::{#exm-lp-space}
#### An $L^1$ function not in $L^2$

Consider the [interval](sets.qmd#def-interval) $(0, 1)$ with the Borel $\sigma$-algebra (@def-borel-sigma-algebra)
and Lebesgue measure $\measure$ (@def-lebesgue-measure).
Define $f : (0, 1) \to \reals$ by $f(x) = x^{-1/2}$.

1. For $p = 1$:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \norm{f}_1
   &= \int_0^1 x^{-1/2} \, dx \\
   &= \sb{2 x^{1/2}}_0^1 \\
   &= 2 \\
   &< \infty,
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   so $f \in \mathcal{L}^1((0, 1), \measure)$.
2. For $p = 2$:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \abs{f(x)}^2
   &= \paren{x^{-1/2}}^2 \\
   &= \frac{1}{x}.
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   The [integral](#def-integral) is:
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   \int_0^1 \frac{1}{x} \, dx
   &= \lim_{\smallconst \to 0^+} \sb{\ln x}_\smallconst^1 \\
   &= \lim_{\smallconst \to 0^+} (-\ln \smallconst) \\
   &= \infty.
   \end{aligned}
   $$
   So $\norm{f}_2 = \infty$, so $f \notin \mathcal{L}^2((0, 1), \measure)$.

This shows that $\mathcal{L}^2 \subset \mathcal{L}^1$ on [sets](sets.qmd#def-set) of [finite measure](#def-finite-measure): a larger $p$ imposes stricter requirements near singularities.

:::
